<!-- ============ HERO ============ -->
<section class="band" style="background:#2E5E4E;">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="eyebrow" style="color:#F2C566 !important;">For parents of children with autism, special needs &amp; food allergies</div>
    <h1 style="font-size:44px; margin-bottom:18px; color:#ffffff !important;">You're not a bad cook. You're a tired parent trying to feed a child who can't eat “normal” food.</h1>
    <p class="lede" style="color:#DCE8DF !important;">The Healing Collection: 90 allergy-free family meals, 30 lunch boxes, 30 gentle detox drinks, printables, party recipes and 31 days of Bible declarations — made by an autism mum who has stood in your kitchen.</p>
    <div class="pills">
      <span style="background:rgba(255,255,255,.12); color:#fff !important;">Gluten-free</span><span style="background:rgba(255,255,255,.12); color:#fff !important;">Dairy-free</span>
      <span style="background:rgba(255,255,255,.12); color:#fff !important;">Corn-free</span><span style="background:rgba(255,255,255,.12); color:#fff !important;">Egg-free</span>
      <span style="background:rgba(255,255,255,.12); color:#fff !important;">Processed-sugar-free</span>
    </div>
    <figure class="pic"><!-- PICTURE 1: bundle image (built in) -->
<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="The Healing Collection — 6 books" style="width:100%;border-radius:18px;box-shadow:0 18px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.18);"></figure>

    <p style="color:#E7EFE9 !important;">It's 6:15pm. You open the fridge for the third time.</p>
    <p style="color:#E7EFE9 !important;">You already know what's going to happen. You'll cook something new, your child will push the plate away, and you'll end up making the same three “safe” foods again. Then you'll cook a separate dinner for everyone else. And tomorrow, you'll do it all again.</p>
    <p style="color:#E7EFE9 !important;">Here's what nobody tells you: <b style="color:#F2C566 !important;">you're not failing.</b> You're trying to cook allergy-free without a plan — reading labels alone, guessing what's safe, and hoping tonight will be different. That's not a parenting problem. It's a <b style="color:#F2C566 !important;">plan problem</b>. And plan problems have simple fixes.</p>

    <div class="btn-row"><a href="#" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="btn">Yes! Give me the Healing Collection<small>All 6 books · just $14.99</small></a></div>
    <p class="trust" style="color:#B9CBBF !important;">✓ Instant download &nbsp; ✓ Phone, tablet or print &nbsp; ✓ Buy from anywhere</p>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ============ DOES THIS SOUND LIKE YOUR HOME? ============ -->
<section class="band" style="background:#1F4136;">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="eyebrow" style="color:#F2C566 !important;">Mama, Papa — I see you</div>
    <h2 style="font-size:32px; margin-bottom:24px; color:#ffffff !important;">Does this sound like your home?</h2>
    <div class="struggle">Your child eats <b>only three or four foods</b> — and you lie awake wondering if they're getting enough.</div>
    <div class="struggle">You stand in the shop <b>reading every label</b>, and still aren't sure what's safe.</div>
    <div class="struggle">You cook <b>one meal for your child</b> and another for everyone else. Every single day.</div>
    <div class="struggle">Family members say <b>“just give them bread, they'll be fine”</b> — and you feel so alone.</div>
    <div class="struggle">The lunch box <b>comes home untouched</b>, and your heart sinks a little more.</div>
    <div class="struggle">Birthday parties end in <b>tears</b>, because there's nothing your child can eat.</div>
    <div class="struggle">Tummy aches, meltdowns, <b>nights that never seem to end</b> — and searching Google at 2am.</div>
    <p style="color:#F2C566 !important; font-family:'Fraunces',serif; font-size:24px; font-weight:600; text-align:center; margin-top:26px;">If you nodded even once, this collection was made for you.</p>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ============ WHAT NOBODY TOLD YOU ============ -->
<section class="band" style="background:#FBF6EC;">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="eyebrow">Here's what nobody told you</div>
    <h2 style="font-size:32px; margin-bottom:28px; color:#2E5E4E !important;">It was never just about “picky eating”.</h2>
    <div class="point"><div class="mark" style="background:#C8643B;">1</div><div><h4>Allergens hide in “safe” foods</h4>
      <p>Pap, custard, Milo, stock cubes, baking powder, soy sauce, many “gluten-free” products — gluten, corn, dairy and sugar hide in foods we eat every day. You can't avoid what you can't see.</p></div></div>
    <div class="point"><div class="mark" style="background:#6FA37A;">2</div><div><h4>A calmer gut can mean a calmer child</h4>
      <p>Many parents notice that when the gut is irritated, everything feels harder — sleep, moods, toilet troubles and picky eating. Removing the irritants and adding healing foods is where many families start.</p></div></div>
    <div class="point"><div class="mark" style="background:#E3A12F;">3</div><div><h4>Picky eating is often about feeling safe</h4>
      <p>A child who eats only a few foods is often a child whose senses feel overwhelmed. Pressure makes it worse. Gentle steps, familiar foods and fun shapes make it better.</p></div></div>
    <figure class="pic"><!-- PICTURE 2: day page from Healing Plates (built in) -->
<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="A day page from Healing Plates" style="width:100%;border-radius:18px;box-shadow:0 18px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.18);"><figcaption>Every day planned: breakfast, lunch and dinner with tick-box ingredients</figcaption></figure>
    <p>Put those together and you get exactly what you're living through. Not a parenting problem — a <b>plan problem</b>. And that's exactly what the Healing Collection gives you.</p>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ============ WHY IT EXISTS (STORY) ============ -->
<section class="band" style="background:#E4EFE3;">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="eyebrow">Why this collection exists</div>
    <h2 style="font-size:30px; margin-bottom:20px; color:#2E5E4E !important;">I have stood in that kitchen too.</h2>
    <p>I'm Tris — an autism mum. I know the child who eats only three foods. The sleepless nights. The quiet ache when the words haven't come yet. The prayers whispered over a sleeping child.</p>
    <p>When I changed what went on my child's plate — taking out gluten, dairy, corn, eggs and processed sugar, cooking real food from scratch, and adding one gentle detox drink a day — things began to change. Slowly at first. Then I saw a <b>real, significant improvement in my child</b>.</p>
    <p>I couldn't keep these recipes to myself. So I put everything into one simple collection: no long science, no fancy ingredients you can't find. Just real food — jollof, yam, plantain, pasta, pancakes, nuggets — made safe for your family, one day at a time.</p>
    <p><b>It's not a promise that every child will respond the same way. It's a plan built around real families, real kitchens and real children — like yours.</b></p>
  </div>
</section>

      <div class="step" data-n="WK 2" style="--c:#C8643B;"><h4>Settle into the routine</h4><p>Lunch boxes your child is proud to open, one gentle detox drink a day, and one weekly shopping list.</p></div>
      <div class="step" data-n="WK 3" style="--c:#6FA37A;"><h4>Try something new</h4><p>Gentle picky-eater tricks, hidden vegetables and fun shapes — and a sticker for every new food tried.</p></div>
      <div class="step" data-n="WK 4" style="--c:#E3A12F;"><h4>Feel the difference</h4><p>Use the food &amp; mood tracker to notice what's changed — sleep, tummies, moods, mealtimes.</p></div>
